_README: Response HEADER sets captured live from api.github.com/search/repositories on
2026-08-14, all UNAUTHENTICATED (no PAT exists on this machine and none was
requested). Header names are lowercased as `fetch` normalizes them; values are
verbatim. Noise headers with no bearing on this adapter (server, date,
content-encoding, the CORS/CSP set, x-github-edge-region, x-github-request-id)
were dropped rather than recorded -- the same trimming
tests/fixtures/github/captured-headers.json applies.
The four response BODIES beside this file are also real, captured in the same
run: search-mcp-created.json (trimmed from 50 items to 12 -- total_count is left
at the real 3644 on purpose, so a test can prove the adapter never mistakes the
server's total for what it actually retrieved), search-netdevops-created.json
(untrimmed -- a whole topic that yields exactly ONE repo once the star floor is
applied), search-empty.json, and search-or-422.json.
WHAT THESE PIN, and why each was captured rather than imagined:
1. NO CONDITIONAL REQUESTS ON SEARCH. `search_200` carries no etag, no
last-modified, and says `cache-control: no-cache`. This is the same finding
tests/fixtures/github/captured-headers.json records for the client, arriving
at the adapter: there is nothing for src/adapters/github.ts to send as an
If-None-Match and nothing to store, so its AdapterResult reports etag and
lastModified as null on every fetch, forever. That is honest reporting, not
an unimplemented feature.
2. GITHUB REJECTS `OR` BETWEEN QUALIFIERS, IN ITS OWN WORDS. `search_422_or` is
the response to `q=topic:llm created:>=2026-02-15 OR pushed:>=2026-07-31` --
HTTP 422, with the body in search-or-422.json saying: "Logical operators only
apply to text, not to qualifiers." §4's `created:>180d OR pushed:>14d` is
therefore not expressible as one query. See src/adapters/github.ts's module
doc comment for how the union is built instead, and what it costs.
3. PAGINATION `link` HEADERS ARE ABSOLUTE URLs on api.github.com, carrying the
`/search/repositories` path. `search_200`'s link header is the real one. This
adapter never follows them (one page per query, by design), but the header is
recorded because src/fetch/github.ts's resource classification depends on that
pathname -- matching on the raw string instead would gate a paginated search
against the 6x-larger `core` budget.
4. THE SEARCH BUDGET IS 10/MIN, AND ITS OWN RESOURCE. `x-ratelimit-limit: 10`
with `x-ratelimit-resource: search`, against `core`'s 60/hour on the very same
client. Nine topics x two queries is 18 requests -- more than an
unauthenticated minute's entire search budget, which is the whole reason the
adapter rotates its query list and stops honestly rather than hammering.
NOT captured, deliberately: a 403/429 rate-limit response. Producing one means
abusing the API to trip a limit, which this project's politeness rule forbids and
the M4a plan explicitly rules out. Tests that need an exhausted budget spread
`search_200` below and override x-ratelimit-remaining/used -- a REAL header shape
with an adjusted counter, flagged as such at each use. Note also that GitHub's
unauthenticated rate-limit BODY names the caller's public IP address, so anything
captured from one would need redacting before it could enter a tracked file (see
tests/fixtures/github/captured-headers.json's graphql_403 for that precedent).

search_200._note: No etag. No last-modified. Deliberately recorded as absent, not omitted for brevity.

search_422_or._note: Body is search-or-422.json. This is GitHub refusing §4's OR, not a client bug.
